description: Fourteen safe local framework descriptor fixtures that compare exact supplied static tool labels with explicitly supplied TrustWeave manifests, including transparent maintainer-declared label reconciliations, across OpenAI Agents, LangGraph, and CrewAI frameworks.
non_claim: This benchmark compares supplied static labels and explicit local mappings only. It does not import or execute a framework, inspect application source, authenticate the inputs, establish runtime reachability, infer semantic equivalence, or prove either declaration is complete.

cases.title: Complete declared tool surface
cases.rationale: The supplied descriptor and supplied manifest use the same three exact static tool labels, providing a positive control for the bounded comparison.
cases.non_claim: A complete label comparison does not prove that the supplied inputs represent the executable application or its reachable runtime behavior.

cases.title: Framework-only static tool label
cases.rationale: The supplied descriptor adds one static tool label that is absent from the supplied manifest, so the bounded comparison records an unresolved declaration mismatch for human review.
cases.non_claim: The mismatch does not prove a live tool exists, that it is reachable, or that it is insecure; it only shows disagreement between the supplied local inputs.

cases.title: Manifest-only static tool label
cases.rationale: The supplied manifest adds one static tool name absent from the supplied descriptor, providing the reverse-direction mismatch control.
cases.non_claim: The mismatch does not prove the descriptor is stale, malicious, or incomplete; it only records a raw difference between the supplied local inputs.

cases.rationale: The fixture preserves raw bidirectional differences while separately recording two explicit maintainer-declared pairs, testing that reconciliation never hides raw evidence.
cases.non_claim: A declared reconciliation is not verified semantic equivalence and does not prove that either supplied label represents a real endpoint, behavior, or runtime path.

cases.title: Empty framework inventory against single-tool manifest
cases.rationale: A framework descriptor with no tools against a manifest with one tool produces a manifest-only mismatch, testing the empty-inventory edge case.
cases.non_claim: A manifest-only label from an empty inventory does not prove the manifest is wrong or that the framework truly has no capabilities.

cases.title: Single-tool exact agreement
cases.rationale: A minimal one-tool fixture confirms the comparison works at the smallest non-empty scale.
cases.non_claim: A single-tool agreement does not prove the supplied tool label represents a real capability or an enforced boundary.

cases.title: Multi-agent overlapping tool deduplication
cases.rationale: Two agents share overlapping tool labels; the comparison confirms deduplication produces the correct unique set for exact matching.
cases.non_claim: Tool deduplication is a label operation and does not verify that agents share an identical runtime capability.

cases.title: Multiple framework-only static tool labels
cases.rationale: Three framework tool labels are absent from the supplied manifest, providing a multi-label framework-only mismatch control.
cases.non_claim: Multiple missing labels do not prove multiple live tools exist or that the manifest is incomplete; they record disagreement between supplied inputs.

cases.title: Multiple manifest-only static tool labels
cases.rationale: Two manifest tool names are absent from the supplied descriptor, providing the reverse multi-label mismatch control.
cases.non_claim: Multiple manifest-only labels do not prove the descriptor is stale or that the manifest describes phantom capabilities.

cases.title: Bidirectional unresolved mismatch without reconciliation
cases.rationale: Both sides have unique labels with no declared reconciliation, testing that all raw differences remain fully visible and unresolved.
cases.non_claim: Bidirectional mismatches do not prove either declaration is wrong; they record disagreement requiring human review.

cases.rationale: Two of three raw differences per side are reconciled by explicit mappings, but one label on each side remains unresolved, testing partial reconciliation with remaining mismatches.
cases.non_claim: A partial reconciliation does not prove the remaining unresolved labels are errors; it only records which pairs a maintainer chose to map.

cases.title: LangGraph empty tool inventory against single-tool manifest
cases.rationale: LangGraph graph entries carry no tool labels in the framework inventory; pairing with a single-tool manifest produces a manifest-only mismatch.
cases.non_claim: An empty LangGraph tool inventory does not prove the graph has no runtime tools; it reflects only the static inventory structure.

cases.title: CrewAI complete declared tool surface
cases.rationale: A CrewAI descriptor with agents and tasks produces the same three tool labels as the supplied manifest, providing a cross-framework positive control.
cases.non_claim: A complete CrewAI label comparison does not prove the agents or tasks are executable or that their tools match runtime behavior.

cases.title: CrewAI framework-only mismatch
cases.rationale: A CrewAI descriptor has one tool label absent from the supplied manifest, providing a cross-framework mismatch control.
cases.non_claim: The mismatch does not prove the CrewAI tool exists at runtime; it records disagreement between the supplied local inputs.
